title: Warning to the Wicked and the Self: Explanation of Misuse Through a Parable and Awakening the Self

questions.question: What main lesson are students told to notice from the comparison at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: Human abilities were not given just to chase worldly comfort like animals do.

questions.question: In the comparison, what was the first servant told to do with the money he received?
questions.answer: He was told to buy clothing made from a certain kind of fabric.

questions.question: How much money did the first servant receive, and what did he do with it?
questions.answer: He got twenty gold coins and bought a very good suit.

questions.question: What two things did the employer give the second servant?
questions.answer: He gave him a large amount of money and a written note.

questions.question: Why would a wise person know that the second servant’s money was not mainly for clothes?
questions.answer: Because a small amount had already been enough to buy excellent clothing, so the much larger amount must have been for a different purpose.

questions.question: What mistake did the second servant make before spending the money?
questions.answer: He failed to read the instructions he had been given.

questions.question: How did the second servant decide what to do instead?
questions.answer: He copied the first servant without understanding his own task.

questions.question: What did the second servant spend all the money on?
questions.answer: He used it all to buy a suit of clothes.

questions.question: What does the poor-quality suit show about the second servant’s choice?
questions.answer: It shows he wasted something valuable and ended up with a bad result.

questions.question: Why was the employer right to scold and punish the second servant?
questions.answer: Because he ignored his duty, wasted the money, and acted foolishly.

questions.question: In the lesson drawn from the comparison, what does the “capital” of life refer to?
questions.answer: It refers to the abilities, gifts, and potential placed in a person’s life.

questions.question: What are people warned not to spend their life’s capital on?
questions.answer: On bodily pleasures and this temporary worldly life.

questions.question: According to the passage, how does a person become worse than animals?
questions.answer: By using greater human gifts only for low desires instead of higher purposes.

questions.question: What contrast does the passage make between human beings and animals?
questions.answer: Humans have much greater resources and responsibility, so lowering themselves to animal-like living is a bigger failure.

questions.question: What is the overall message of the whole comparison?
questions.answer: A person should use life’s gifts for their real purpose, not waste them on short-lived pleasure.

questions.question: What does the passage ask the reader to examine carefully?
questions.answer: A comparison meant to explain the real purpose of human faculties.

questions.question: According to that comparison, what are human faculties not meant for?
questions.answer: They are not meant only for gaining worldly benefits like an animal.

questions.question: Who gave the money in the comparison?
questions.answer: An employer gave it to his servants.

questions.question: What was special about the second servant’s situation compared with the first?
questions.answer: He received far more money and also got written directions.

questions.question: What should the second servant have understood from receiving much more than the first servant?
questions.answer: He should have understood that he had a larger and more important assignment.

questions.question: What clue did the second servant ignore that could have guided him correctly?
questions.answer: He ignored the note placed in his pocket.

questions.question: What wrong method did the second servant use in making his decision?
questions.answer: He judged by copying someone else instead of following his own instructions.

questions.question: What result came from spending all the money on clothes?
questions.answer: He got an inferior suit and failed in the task he had been sent to do.

questions.question: What does the comparison suggest about using something valuable for a low goal?
questions.answer: It is misuse and shows poor judgment.

questions.question: Why is the second servant described as foolish?
questions.answer: Because he had the means and directions to do something important, but he wasted both.

questions.question: In the warning that follows, who is directly addressed?
questions.answer: The speaker addresses the self and a close companion.

questions.question: What kind of pleasures are criticized in the warning?
questions.answer: Physical cravings and temporary enjoyments.

questions.question: Why is following such pleasures especially serious for human beings?
questions.answer: Because humans have greater abilities than animals and are supposed to use them better.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying a person can fall below even the lowest animal?
questions.answer: A person can misuse human gifts so badly that morally he ends up in a lower state than creatures with less responsibility.

questions.question: What practical advice does the passage give to the reader?
questions.answer: Wake up, use your abilities wisely, and do not waste life on passing desires.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the story about the two servants?
questions.answer: It teaches that people should understand the true purpose of the gifts given to them.

questions.question: What did the first servant successfully do with a small amount of money?
questions.answer: He bought a high-quality outfit.

questions.question: What does that first purchase help prove about the second servant’s larger amount?
questions.answer: It proves the larger amount was meant for something beyond simple clothing.

questions.question: What extra responsibility came with the paper placed in the second servant’s pocket?
questions.answer: He was expected to learn and carry out a specific assignment.

questions.question: What basic failure led to the second servant’s bigger failure?
questions.answer: He did not pay attention to the instructions.

questions.question: How did comparing himself to the first servant lead him in the wrong direction?
questions.answer: He assumed both had the same purpose when they did not.

questions.question: What is ironic about the second servant’s final purchase?
questions.answer: He spent much more money yet ended up with something much worse.

questions.question: What does the employer’s anger show about neglecting a trust?
questions.answer: It shows that wasting a serious trust deserves blame.

questions.question: How is the story connected to human life?
questions.answer: Human life also contains valuable gifts that must be used for their true purpose.

questions.question: What are “the capital and potentialities” of life?
questions.answer: They are the resources, talents, and abilities a person has been given.

questions.question: What false use of these gifts is rejected in the passage?
questions.answer: Using them only for temporary worldly enjoyment and bodily appetite.

questions.question: How does the passage describe living only for appetite?
questions.answer: It describes it as acting like an animal, or even worse.

questions.question: Why does the passage say a human is far above the highest animal?
questions.answer: Because a human has much greater gifts and possibilities.

questions.question: If a human uses those gifts wrongly, what makes the fall especially severe?
questions.answer: The fall is severe because the person turns great blessings into a cause of disgrace.

questions.question: What main warning should an eighth-grade student take from this passage?
questions.answer: Do not waste your mind, heart, and abilities on low goals; use them for the higher purpose they were given for.

questions.question: What claim about human life is made in the opening sentence of the target passage?
questions.answer: Human powers were not given merely to gain worldly living in an animal-like way.

questions.question: In the comparison, why is the first servant included at all?
questions.answer: He gives a clear example that a small amount can already cover the cost of fine clothing.

questions.question: What does the thousand gold pieces suggest about the second servant’s mission?
questions.answer: It suggests his mission was larger and more important than buying clothes.

questions.question: Why was the written paper important to the second servant’s duty?
questions.answer: It contained directions he needed in order to use the money properly.

questions.question: What does the second servant reveal about himself by not reading the paper?
questions.answer: He shows carelessness and lack of understanding.

questions.question: What poor decision did he make after looking at the first servant?
questions.answer: He copied the same action without thinking about the difference in their tasks.

questions.question: What was wrong not only with what he bought, but with how he thought?
questions.answer: He acted without reflection and ignored the purpose behind what he had been given.

questions.question: How does the comparison show the difference between appearance and purpose?
questions.answer: Clothes may look important, but the real issue is whether the money was used for the right goal.

questions.question: Why is the employer’s punishment presented as justified?
questions.answer: Because the servant failed both in obedience and in wise use of what was entrusted to him.

questions.question: After the comparison, what direct command is given to the self and the friend?
questions.answer: They are told to wake up and act sensibly.

questions.question: What are readers warned not to imitate?
questions.answer: They are warned not to live for bodily desire the way animals do.

questions.question: What does the phrase about fleeting life teach about worldly pleasure?
questions.answer: It teaches that worldly pleasure is brief and not worth making it life’s main goal.

questions.question: What does being “superior in capital” mean in this passage?
questions.answer: It means humans have richer abilities and greater inner resources than animals.

questions.question: What happens when a person with higher gifts chooses lower aims?
questions.answer: That person drops beneath the level he was meant to live at.

questions.question: State the central moral of the passage in one sentence.
questions.answer: The gifts of human life must be used for meaningful higher purposes, not wasted on temporary desires.

questions.question: What does the comparison ask the reader to understand about human faculties?
questions.answer: They have a greater purpose than simply helping a person survive or enjoy worldly life.

questions.question: What job was simple and limited in the comparison?
questions.answer: Buying a suit with a small amount of money.

questions.question: What showed that the second servant had a broader mission?
questions.answer: He received a much larger sum and a written message.

questions.question: What should the second servant have done first after receiving the paper?
questions.answer: He should have read it to learn what he was supposed to do.

questions.question: What kind of thinking mistake did he make?
questions.answer: He assumed his role was the same as another servant’s role.

questions.question: Why is it important that the first servant already bought excellent clothing with little money?
questions.answer: It proves the second servant’s large amount was intended for something beyond that.

questions.question: How did the second servant misuse trust?
questions.answer: He spent what was entrusted to him on the wrong purpose.

questions.question: What does getting a much worse suit after spending more money teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that having more resources does not help if they are used foolishly.

questions.question: What does the employer’s reaction teach about responsibility?
questions.answer: Greater gifts bring greater accountability.

questions.question: In the warning section, what does “capital” most likely mean?
questions.answer: It means the valuable assets of life, like one’s abilities and opportunities.

questions.question: What is meant by “potentialities” in this passage?
questions.answer: The capacities a person could develop and use for the right purpose.

questions.question: Which lifestyle is condemned in the final warning?
questions.answer: A life centered on physical pleasure and short-term worldly enjoyment.

questions.question: How does the passage use animals as a comparison?
questions.answer: It says that living only for appetite reduces a human to an animal-like level.

questions.question: Why is falling below animals described as possible for a human?
questions.answer: Because a human can betray greater gifts by choosing lower goals.

questions.question: What is one strong life lesson a Muslim student can take from this passage?
questions.answer: Allah-given abilities should be used responsibly for higher meaning, not wasted on desires that quickly pass.

questions.question: What is the reader told to do with the comparison in this passage?
questions.answer: The reader is told to think deeply about its meaning.

questions.question: What false idea about life is the comparison correcting?
questions.answer: The idea that human gifts are only for worldly gain and physical comfort.

questions.question: How much money did the two servants receive, and why does that difference matter?
questions.answer: One received twenty gold coins and the other received a thousand, showing they were not given the same level of task.

questions.question: What common-sense conclusion should be made from that difference?
questions.answer: The larger amount must have been meant for something more important than clothing.

questions.question: What added guidance was given to the second servant besides the money?
questions.answer: He was also given written instructions.

questions.question: What was the second servant’s first serious mistake?
questions.answer: He did not check the instructions meant to guide him.

questions.question: What was his second serious mistake?
questions.answer: He copied another servant instead of understanding his own duty.

questions.question: What does his purchase reveal about waste?
questions.answer: It shows that a person can waste great resources and still end up with something poor.

questions.question: Why is the punishment in the comparison not presented as unfair?
questions.answer: Because the servant’s failure came from his own careless and foolish choices.

questions.question: Who is being warned in the paragraph after the comparison?
questions.answer: The speaker’s own self and the person listening are both being warned.

questions.question: What human possessions are compared to the servant’s money?
questions.answer: A person’s life resources, abilities, and possibilities.

questions.question: What are these gifts not supposed to be spent on?
questions.answer: They are not supposed to be consumed only by bodily urges and passing worldly pleasures.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about human dignity?
questions.answer: Human dignity depends on using one’s greater gifts in a worthy way.

questions.question: According to the passage, what causes a human to sink very low?
questions.answer: Misusing high human capacities for low animal-like desires.

questions.question: Summarize the passage’s warning in your own words.
questions.answer: If you use your Allah-given abilities only for temporary pleasure, you waste your life and fall below the level you were created for.
